draft.title: Choosing a mix of methods
card: A research method is a way of collecting information. Questionnaires, interviews and observation are three examples.
information in numbers, such as how many people agree with a statement. A questionnaire with set answers often gives this.
information in words, such as how a person feels and why. An interview often gives this.
Each method has weaknesses. Using more than one method lets the findings be compared and checked against each other, so they are stronger and more balanced.
draft.remember: One method gives one view. A mix of methods gives findings that can be checked against each other.

a.q: Why is using a questionnaire and interviews together often better than using only a questionnaire?
opts: The findings can be compared and checked against each other
The project then needs no resource list at the end
Interviews always give more accurate results than surveys
Two methods remove the need to choose a research topic
a.why: Each method has weaknesses, and a second method can check or add to the first. The claim that interviews are always more accurate is wrong, because the card says every method has weaknesses.
a.clue: Think about what a second method adds to the first.

b.q: Ravi studies how teenagers in Penrith feel about social media. His questionnaire shows 70% say it harms their sleep, but he does not know why. Which step best improves his findings?
opts: Interview a few teenagers to learn their reasons
Hand out the same questionnaire to more teenagers
Remove the question about sleep from the questionnaire
Read only websites that agree with the 70% result
b.why: The questionnaire gives numbers but not reasons. Interviews give words that explain why, so the two methods together are more balanced. Repeating the questionnaire gives more numbers of the same kind, so the gap stays.
b.clue: What kind of information is missing: numbers or reasons?

a.best: The findings can be compared and checked against each other

b.best: Interview a few teenagers to learn their reasons
